Further along the same stem, a goldfinch hangs upside down off a head, eating the seed straight out of it, entirely unbothered, its red-masked face tilted sideways, a rival finishing the job first.
Back at the rim behind, two adult fae in copper-red and teal point opposite directions into the wind, both absolutely certain, while thirty white tufts stream past between their outstretched arms.
Out on the bough behind, a jay lands with its beak already crammed full, its blue blade-ribs bright, eyeing the stem with the focused calm of somebody who arrived second and still won.

Further back along the same stem, a long-limbed woman in amber-dyed rush-cloth, black hair coiled tight, moth-furred wings clamped flat, bumps a bulging woven-grass sack down each ridge ahead of her, one step at a time.
Down in the tangle below, a dormouse presses both cheeks out solid, unable to close its mouth, sitting back on its haunches with its round tail curled up, deep in a drift of streaming white down.

Further along behind, a slender man in plum and ochre bark-cloth, copper hair loose, dragonfly-clear wings akimbo, holds a woven-grass net out in completely the wrong direction while a hundred tufts bolt past the other way.
Out on the bough further back, a squirrel grips one seed in both paws with both cheeks already packed solid, its amber tail flung forward over its own head by the same gust hitting everything else.
Back at the rim behind, three adult fae haul a grass cord with only heads and shoulders showing over the edge, all leaning back hard in a row, the last one sitting flat down on the job.

Further along the stem behind, a shrew works through a deep drift of white down underfoot on entirely its own business, its pointed nose going side to side, tufts parting around its shoulders like a small prow.

Further back on the same stem, a narrow-shouldered woman in rose-gold petal-silk, red hair pinned with a thorn, leaf-veined wings spread for balance, clings with both ankles while a full nutshell-and-river-pebble lid rattles under one hand.

Out on the bough behind, a beetle walks away with a single papery blade-seed as long as her arm laid across its back, the papery blade fanning up in the gusts, the beetle entirely committed to the direction it chose.

Further off along the stem, a long-legged man in indigo bark-cloth, white hair loose, moth-furred amber wings, has climbed three hand-spans higher than anyone needed to, purely to be the highest, and is looking down with satisfaction.

Back at the rim behind, a woman in ember-orange rush-cloth, dark braid whipping sideways, teal dragonfly wings pinned flat by the wind, lies on her back with a full woven-grass sack across her chest, finished, one boot already sailing away.

Further along the stem, a goldfinch and a long-limbed man in russet reach the same head at the same instant, both gripping it, neither giving, the man's copper-veined wings straining, the goldfinch's beak already closing on a seed.

Down in the deep drift below, a dormouse sleeps entirely buried in a mound of streaming white down, its tail the only thing still visible, curling up out of the mass and blowing sideways in the same gust as everything else.

Further back on the bough, a slender woman in ochre and plum, black hair wrapped in a grass cord, amber moth-furred wings spread wide, uses both arms to hold a folded-leaf pail shut while the lashed-leaf lid strains upward.
Out along the stem behind, a jay hops sideways with its beak crammed, eyeing a second seed the size of the fae's head wedged in a fork, doing the calculation, beak too full, trying anyway.

Further along behind, two adult fae in copper and cream share one papery blade-seed as long as both their arms, each gripping an end, walking opposite ways, neither noticing, the papery blade bowing between them.

Back at the rim, a long-limbed man in teal rush-cloth, auburn hair loose, clear-veined wings flat in the gust, is wrapped to both eyes in a sash of caught white down, still walking, entirely furred over, still carrying.

Further off along the stem, a squirrel has tucked eight papery blade-seeds into the fur of its chest and both haunches, grips a ninth in its paws, and is eyeing the stem above with the expression of a creature making a plan.

Down in the tangle below, a shrew has seized a papery blade-seed as long as its own body and is hauling it backward through the down-drift with all four legs, going somewhere specific, entirely uninterested in negotiation.

Further along the same stem behind, a narrow woman in rose-gold petal-silk, silver hair loose, gold-dusted wings catching every gust, holds a woven-grass net wide open facing directly upwind while everything that matters streams past behind her.

Out on the bough behind, a man in amber and indigo bark-cloth, dark hair in a short plait, dragonfly-clear wings folded, sits cross-legged on his full woven-grass sack, river pebble on the lid, arms folded, watching everyone else still working.

Back at the rim, a goldfinch and a long-limbed woman in copper-dyed rush-cloth reach the same last three tufts together, the goldfinch plucking the first, the woman's cupped hands closing on the second, the third already bolting in the gust.

Further along the stem, a dormouse grips the woody stalk with its back legs and stretches its whole body out sideways after a stream of a hundred white tufts bolting past, both forepaws open, catching exactly none.
